column1: Machines. The 'National Health Call Center’ (Shyastho Batayan)
accessed by dialing ‘16263’ has been launched to provide
healthcare services to the citizens. It is possible to receive public
complaints through SMS and take specific measures according to
the grievances through the “Grievance Redress System (GRS)” in
government hospitals. Advanced telemedicine services are being
provided in 96 hospitals. A video conferencing system has been set
up in all Medical Colleges and Specialized Hospitals, Divisional
and District health offices, District Hospitals, and Upazila
Hospitals. Under the Health Strengthening System (HSS), the
"Health Minister National Award" is being given to better
performing health institutions in the country to encourage them to
play a more dynamic and effective role in the health sector. HIS
and e-Health operation plan also implementing the supply chain
management system which has a number of modules that include
equipment tracker e-AMS and eLMIS, at the national and
subnational level.
Bangladesh has harnessed impressive rollout of eHealth in its
public health sector, as a first nation in the world to announce
"Digital Bangladesh 2021” vision in 2009.
Family welfare has been taking various contemporary initiatives
to successfully implement the government's intention to deliver
digital health services to the doorsteps of the people with the aim
of building Smart Bangladesh and implementing the Government's
Vision 2041.
column2: Bangladesh has made remarkable progress in all

column1: areas of eHealth including connectivity; data gathering, generating
evidence and response, telemedicine; public accountability; round
the clock health call center; sms broadcast for citizen campaigns;
project for universal electronic health records and hospital
automation; human resource management and information
system; licensing of health facilities, routine weekly teleconference
among all health managers in all tiers concurrently to conduct
management meetings and monitor and review national and
subnational health situation; use of social media in boosting staff
empowerment, motivation and skills, and educating public on
health; summarization and display of data real time in visually
impressive web dashboards; etc. Under the 4th sector-wide
program called Health, Population and Nutrition Sector Program
(HPNSP 2017-2023), the activities are being continued under the
HIS and e-Health Operational Plan.
